newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOBSLEIGH-LUEDERS TAKES WORLD CUP WITH FINAL RACE WIN.
newsitem.headline: BOBSLEIGH-LUEDERS TAKES WORLD CUP WITH FINAL RACE WIN.

text.p: Canada's Pierre Lueders won the season's final World Cup two-man bobsleigh race on Saturday to narrowly clinch the overall title.
Lueders and brakeman Dave MacEachern clocked the fastest times in both heats down the 1.36-km Spiral track to finish in a two-run combined time of one minute 48.43 seconds.
"Our first start wasn't very good," said Lueders. "We ran too far and that cost us velocity. In the second run we let the sled run better and did less driving."
Tied for second 0.48 seconds behind were Reto Goetschi and Guido Acklin of Switzerland and Jim Herberich and John Kasper of the United States.
Lueders and Guenther Huber of Italy both finished the season with 224 points but the 26-year-old Canadian edged out Huber for the title with four wins from seven races.
American Brian Shimer placed third with 190 points after finishing fourth on Saturday in 1:48.96 with brakeman Robert Olesen.
Lueders, World Cup runner-up last year, won the season's opener at Altenberg, Germany, in November and added victories at La Plagne, France, in December, and Calgary, Canada, last week.
Huber, who placed fifth on Saturday, had a single win at Konigssee, Germany, last month.
"Lueders had four big victories and I had only one, so it's fair," said Huber, two-man bronze medallist at the 1994 Lillehammer Olympics. "He was better."
